findings.title: 2 selectors with high match cost
findings.action: Universal selectors, long descendant chains and :has()/:not() are matched right-to-left against many elements. Prefer a single class on the target element.

findings.title: Large DOM (6,124 nodes)
findings.evidence: 6,124 elements, maximum depth 9. Heaviest subtree: html (6,123 nodes).
findings.action: Every node is re-examined on style recalculation and layout. Paginate long lists, virtualise tables, and remove wrapper elements that exist only for styling.

findings.title: Large DOM (24,385 nodes)
findings.evidence: 24,385 elements, maximum depth 13. Heaviest subtree: html (24,384 nodes).
findings.action: Every node is re-examined on style recalculation and layout. Paginate long lists, virtualise tables, and remove wrapper elements that exist only for styling.

findings.title: 199 elements with animations or transitions
findings.evidence: 199 elements have a non-zero animation or transition.
findings.action: Running animations keep the refresh driver and compositor awake, drawing power even when nothing is interacting. Prefer transform/opacity, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.

findings.title: 3 selectors with high match cost
findings.evidence: * (universal selector); .priority-table thead th.axe-col-header .priority-sort-btn (deep descendant chain); .priority-table thead th.axe-col-header .priority-sort-btn:hover (deep descendant chain)
